skill.name: video-edit
skill.description: Routes video editing requests to Wan 2.7, Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control, or Lucy Edit Restyle through the RunComfy CLI. Supports restyling, background swaps, packaging changes, motion transfer, outfit edits, and audio preservation.
skill.summary: Select a RunComfy model and prepare focused instructions for an existing video edit.
skill.author: skills-collective

security_audit.summary: All 67 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, example URLs, or documentation of credential storage. Separate review found shell-construction, unpinned dependency, and third-party media disclosure risks that require clear safeguards.

remediation.issue: Generated prompts are embedded in shell-quoted JSON without a mandatory safe serialization procedure.
remediation.suggestion: Build input with a JSON serializer and execute the CLI with an argument array. Never concatenate user-controlled text into a shell command.

remediation.issue: The prerequisite installs an unversioned CLI package globally.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed CLI version and document package provenance and integrity verification before installation.

remediation.issue: Prompts and media URLs are sent to RunComfy, and its servers fetch referenced media.
remediation.suggestion: Require user approval before transfer, warn against sensitive media, and recommend short-lived access-controlled URLs.

content.user_title: Edit Videos with Intent-Routed AI Models
content.value_statement: Choosing the wrong video model wastes time and produces inconsistent edits. This skill selects a suitable RunComfy model and builds model-specific instructions.
actual_capabilities: Routes general restyling, background swaps, and packaging edits to Wan 2.7 Edit-Video.
Routes reference-driven character motion transfer to Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control.
Routes lightweight outfit, lighting, and atmospheric changes to Lucy Edit Restyle.
Builds model-specific prompts that prioritize identity, motion, framing, or audio preservation.
Invokes the selected model through the RunComfy CLI and downloads generated outputs.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, an authenticated RunComfy account, and internet access.
Source videos and reference images must be available through URLs accepted by the selected model.
Each invocation uses one model and inherits that model's duration, resolution, and aspect constraints.
The skill provides generative transformations, not manual timeline editing or frame-level correction.

use_cases.title: Restyle Talking-Head Clips
use_cases.description: Preserve a speaker's face, motion, lip movement, and audio while changing the setting or visual treatment.

use_cases.title: Update Product Visuals
use_cases.description: Replace packaging or backgrounds while retaining original framing, hand movement, and camera motion.

use_cases.title: Transfer Character Motion
use_cases.description: Apply motion from a reference clip to a target character while maintaining identity and spatial constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Video Restyle
prompt_templates.prompt: Restyle [video URL] with [visual change]. Preserve the subject's face and motion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused outfit, lighting, or atmospheric change.

prompt_templates.title: Background Edit with Audio
prompt_templates.prompt: Change the background in [video URL] to [new setting]. Preserve face, pose, lip movement, framing, and original audio.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for talking-head or presenter footage.

prompt_templates.title: Reference Packaging Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [reference image URL] to replace the packaging in [video URL]. Preserve hand movement, camera motion, framing, and original audio.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a specific product design must appear in the source video.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Motion Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Transfer motion from [reference video URL] to the character in [target image or video URL]. Keep [sound preference] and maintain [spatial constraints].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when precise reference motion is more important than general restyling.

output_examples.input: Give a presenter video a modern office background while preserving speech and lip movement.
output: Selected Wan 2.7 Edit-Video for identity-preserving background replacement.
The edit instruction prioritizes face, pose, lip movement, framing, and original audio.

output_examples.input: Apply a dance clip's motion to a character image and keep the source sound.
output: Selected Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control for reference-driven motion transfer.
The request uses image orientation and preserves the reference video's sound.

output_examples.input: Change a walking subject's outfit to business attire without changing the face.
output: Selected Lucy Edit Restyle for a localized outfit change.
The instruction preserves face and motion while limiting the edit to clothing.

best_practices: State preservation requirements before describing the requested change.
Request one visual change per invocation to reduce temporal drift.
Confirm model limits and obtain approval before sending media to RunComfy.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated background, outfit, character, and motion changes in one request.
Do not use Lucy Edit Restyle for complete character replacement or precise motion transfer.
Do not place sensitive media at public URLs or concatenate untrusted text into shell commands.

faq.question: Which model is selected by default?
faq.answer: Wan 2.7 Edit-Video is the default because it supports versatile edits and resolutions up to 1080p.

faq.question: Can the skill preserve original audio?
faq.answer: Yes. Wan and Kling provide audio preservation options when the selected route supports them.

faq.question: Can it transfer motion from another video?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill selects Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control for reference-driven character motion.

faq.question: Does it accept local video files?
faq.answer: The documented routes require source and reference URLs accepted by RunComfy.

faq.question: What are the main output limits?
faq.answer: Wan supports 2 to 10 seconds, Kling supports up to 30 seconds, and Lucy is limited to 720p.

faq.question: Where is media processed?
faq.answer: RunComfy receives the model request, fetches referenced media, performs the edit, and returns output for download.
